locator.panel: loss of C2H5*, product printed second: [C3H7C(CH3)=OH]+ m/z 87, 50%

evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s) for this pathway; moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). ARC COUNT, verified by zooming the scan: the single structure carries FOUR arcs in total - one SOLID fishhook from the odd electron drawn as '+.' on the hydroxyl oxygen, ending with a half-arrowhead (barb) on the C-O bond, plus THREE DASHED fishhooks that each start at one of the three alpha C-C bonds (C-CH3 from above, C-C3H7 and C-C2H5 from below) and end with a barb on that same C-O bond. The three dashed arcs are the three competing alpha cleavages superimposed on one drawing; this record takes the two arcs of the C-C2H5 channel (the shared solid oxygen hook = move 1, the dashed C(1)-C(5) hook = move 2). The third electron of the homolysis, the one that departs with the ethyl radical, is NOT drawn - the book prints only the resulting ion. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the page places both the charge and the odd electron on oxygen ('+.' beside OH), and the precursor SMILES writes that literally as [OH+:8] with two bonds and one unpaired electron. Loss of the ethyl radical is the intermediate-rate channel of the three: m/z 73 (100%) > m/z 87 (50%) > m/z 101 (10%), i.e. the larger the expelled radical the faster the cleavage.

Cross-linked MOD rule variable: IMS_4_17_2 '[C]1([C]2[C]3[C]4)([C]5[C]6)([C]7)([O+.]8)>>[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]1([C]7)[O+.]8.[C]5[C]6'. VERIFIED, not asserted. (i) Left side identical to the other 4.17 variants and an exact match to this record's precursor: RDKit substructure test of the equivalent SMARTS [#6]([#6][#6][#6])([#6][#6])([#6])[O+] against the precursor SMILES returns True with a single match mapping the rule's 2-4/5-6/7/8 onto propyl/ethyl/methyl/oxygen. The product side keeps the propyl (C2C3C4) and the methyl (C7) on C1 and expels C5C6, so this is unambiguously the ethyl-loss, m/z 87 channel of the equation. (ii) Right side is MIS-ENCODED relative to the book in the same way as IMS_4_17_1: the oxygen is still written [O+.]8 SINGLY bonded to C1, so no C=O(+) pi bond is formed and the odd electron stays on oxygen instead of leaving with the alkyl, and the departing ethyl is written [C]5[C]6 rather than [C.]5[C]6. Composition and m/z of the ion come out right (C5H11O, +1, m/z 87) but its electronic structure is an odd-electron species with a three-coordinate, unlabelled carbinol carbon rather than the book's even-electron oxocarbenium [C3H7C(CH3)=OH]+. The conservation guardrail in rules/__init__.py passes it because atoms, total charge (+1 -> +1) and total unpaired count (1 -> 1) are all numerically unchanged; the defect is that the unpaired electron is on the wrong atom and the pi bond is missing.
